tutorial.step1Body: Digits appear one at a time. Watch carefully — you'll need to enter them back.
tutorial.step2Body: After all digits are shown, tap each digit in the same order. In Backward mode, enter them in reverse order.
tutorial.step3Body: Get it right and the sequence grows longer. The game ends after 10 rounds.

tutorial.step1Body: Blocks will flash in a sequence. Watch carefully — you'll need to repeat it.
tutorial.step2Body: After the sequence ends, tap each block in the exact same order it was shown.
tutorial.step3Body: Get it right and the sequence grows longer. The game ends after 10 rounds.

tutorial.step1Body: Stimuli appear one at a time. Decide whether each one matches the stimulus from N steps earlier.
tutorial.step2Body: Tap Match (or press Space / M) when the current stimulus matches the one N steps ago. If it does not match, do nothing.
tutorial.step3Body: If you respond accurately the N-Back level increases. If you struggle it decreases. Stay near your limit.

tutorial.step1Body: A grid of highlighted cells will appear briefly. Study it — you'll need to reproduce it.
tutorial.step2Body: After the grid clears, tap every cell that was highlighted. Use arrow keys to navigate, Space or Enter to toggle.
tutorial.step3Body: Get it right and more cells are added. Get it wrong twice in a row and the count drops. Game ends after 10 rounds.

tutorial.step1Body: An abstract shape and a word appear together. Study each pair carefully — you'll need to recall which word went with each shape.
tutorial.step2Body: A shape appears alone. Tap the word it was paired with from the four options shown.
tutorial.step3Body: Get all pairs right and more pairs are added next round. Make mistakes twice in a row and the number drops. Complete 6 rounds.

tutorial.step1Body: Problems appear one at a time. Type the answer using your keyboard or the on-screen keypad. Work as fast as you can!
tutorial.step2Body: Your answer submits automatically when you've typed enough digits. For negative answers, type the minus sign first.
tutorial.step3Body: Answer 3 correct in a row and problems get harder. Miss 2 in a row and they get easier. You have 60 seconds — go!

tutorial.step1Body: A starting number appears, then arithmetic operations one by one. Keep the running total in your head.
tutorial.step2Body: After the last operation, enter what the final result is. You will not see the intermediate steps.
tutorial.step3Body: A correct answer adds one more step to the chain. Two errors in a row and the chain shortens. Complete 10 rounds.

tutorial.step1Body: An arithmetic equation appears on screen. Decide as fast as you can whether it is correct or not.
tutorial.step2Body: Press T or the left button for True, F or the right button for False. Arrow keys follow the visual button positions.
tutorial.step3Body: Each equation has a time limit. Answering quickly and accurately tightens the pressure. You have 30 equations.

patternMatrix.memorySystem: Trains visual pattern memory — the ability to encode and recall the spatial layout of a grid pattern.
patternMatrix.researchBasis: Based on the Visual Pattern Test (Della Sala et al., 1997), a widely used measure of visual short-term memory that separates spatial from verbal encoding.
patternMatrix.evidenceNote: Consistent practice on this task reliably improves performance on the task itself. Transfer to everyday visual abilities or other cognitive domains is debated in the research literature and has not been definitively established. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.

digitSpan.memorySystem: Trains verbal short-term memory and working memory — the ability to hold and mentally manipulate sequences of spoken or written digits.
digitSpan.researchBasis: Based on the Digit Span subtest of the Wechsler intelligence scales and broader research on phonological loop capacity (Baddeley & Hitch, 1974). One of the most widely used measures of verbal short-term memory capacity in clinical and research settings.
digitSpan.evidenceNote: Consistent practice on this task reliably improves performance on the task itself. Transfer to general memory, academic performance, or other cognitive domains is debated in the research literature and has not been definitively established. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.

nBack.memorySystem: Trains working memory updating — the ability to hold and continuously update information over seconds.
nBack.researchBasis: Based on the N-Back task (Kirchner, 1958), widely used in working memory research and cognitive assessment.
nBack.evidenceNote: Consistent practice reliably improves N-Back performance. Whether gains transfer to general working memory or everyday cognitive abilities remains actively debated in the literature.

pairedAssociates.memorySystem: Trains associative memory — the ability to form and retrieve arbitrary links between unrelated items.
pairedAssociates.researchBasis: Based on the Paired Associates Learning paradigm, used extensively in neuropsychological assessment (e.g., Baddeley et al., 1994) and as a sensitive measure of hippocampal-dependent memory.
pairedAssociates.evidenceNote: Consistent practice on this task reliably improves performance on the task itself. Transfer to everyday memory or other cognitive domains is debated in the research literature and has not been definitively established. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.

arithmeticBlitz.memorySystem: Trains mental arithmetic speed and numerical fluency — the ability to rapidly execute arithmetic operations without paper or calculator.
arithmeticBlitz.researchBasis: Based on mental arithmetic research linking numerical fluency to working memory capacity and executive function (Hitch, 1978; Ashcraft & Stazyk, 1981). Timed arithmetic tasks are used as measures of processing speed in cognitive assessments.
arithmeticBlitz.evidenceNote: Consistent practice on timed arithmetic reliably improves mental calculation speed. Transfer to general mathematical ability, academic performance, or other cognitive domains is debated in the literature. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.

corsiBlocks.memorySystem: Trains visuospatial short-term memory — the ability to hold and mentally manipulate spatial locations.
corsiBlocks.researchBasis: Based on the Corsi Block-Tapping Test (Corsi, 1972; Milner, 1971), a standard neuropsychological measure of visuospatial span widely used in clinical and research settings.
corsiBlocks.evidenceNote: Consistent practice on this task reliably improves performance on the task itself. Transfer to everyday visuospatial abilities or other cognitive domains is debated in the research literature and has not been definitively established. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.

arithmeticChain.memorySystem: Trains working memory and mental arithmetic: you must hold and update a running total in mind while processing each new operation.
arithmeticChain.researchBasis: Based on complex-span and updating paradigms used in working memory research. Requires simultaneous storage and processing, placing heavy demands on the central executive component of working memory.
arithmeticChain.evidenceNote: Consistent practice on this task reliably improves performance on similar mental arithmetic tasks. Transfer to general working memory capacity or other cognitive domains is not established. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.

arithmeticTof.memorySystem: Trains inhibitory control and processing speed — the ability to quickly verify arithmetic statements and suppress impulsive responses under time pressure.
arithmeticTof.researchBasis: Based on arithmetic verification tasks widely used in cognitive psychology. Verification speed correlates with working memory capacity and numerical fluency (Zbrodoff & Logan, 2005).
arithmeticTof.evidenceNote: Consistent practice reliably improves arithmetic verification speed. Transfer to general mathematical ability or other cognitive domains remains under investigation. This app does not claim to raise IQ, prevent cognitive decline, or improve general intelligence.
